Parse crept across the arena, arrow in hand.  Her eyes darted from obstacle to obstacle, her every sense alert to the slightest hint of motion.  "I know you well, robot.  I've studied your code.  Every algorithm, every subroutine.  I can anticipate every move you make, every move you are capable of making.  This can only end one way."

"Well-reasoned, Kim Howell," the mechanical voice echoed from a point not far away.  Parse was instantly in motion.  "Your calculations are flawless, as always.  But any calculation will fail when based on false assumptions."

Parse was only half-listening; the voice emanated from just beyond the next pile of crates.  She crept along quietly as the voice continued.  "You know my computer programming, yes, the code of Omnitron.  But I am not Omnitron anymore.  I am Omnitron-U.  The "U" comes from Unity.  My friend.  She is a part of me now.  And that part is human."

The arrow flew from Parse's hand and struck true with a satisfying crunch of machinery.  But what was it she'd hit?  She picked it up.  Part of a... toy dinosaur?  Why would a robot.... Belatedly, she realized what Omnitron-U had been saying.  Of course, no computer would have thought of such a diversion, given the limited resources in the arena.  He stood behind her now, weapons bristling.  She raised her hands in surrender.

"Our friends are always a part of us, Kim Howell."  The voice, slightly garbled now, still came from the toy.  Omnitron-U reached around, took a component out of it, and inserted it under his "chin."  "It is a lesson I am still learning."

"I never had any friends," Parse murmured, half to herself, still not really thinking of the robot as a person.

"Perhaps it is time for that to change, Kim.  But for now, it is time for you to return home."

Zhu Long and Infinitor seemed promising, though.  We don't know much about Zhu Long's combat ability, but he's smart as heck, can deal several different damage types, and turns into a huge honking dragon.  Infinitor may be nuts, but his manifestations can do just about anything (not just multiple damage types, but might also restrain Progeny or do other stuff), plus, my reasoning at the time went, he can also encase himself in one giant manifestation that looks like it could go toe-to-toe with Progeny.  I picked Infinitor.

I was pretty darn happy when I got through the Captain Cosmic podcast episode.  Avoiding spoilers because it's recent and not that thread, but revelations therein made it seem a lot more likely that Infinitor and Progeny would be evenly matched, plus the psychological aspect of it works out dramatically.  I could still easily be wrong but I'm comfortable with my choice.

I personally don't see how Skinwalker Gloomweaver would have a chance against Progeny.  It's not the Rotting God form, just his front side, which isn't a huge threat.  Lifeline or the Blood Countess could make short work of him for sure (as Lifeline does in fact, very soon).

I had Lifeline win because my guess was that the point of the story (other than selling a ton of comics) was for Lifeline to prove to Jansa and everyone else that he's a hero now and can protect the world from OblivAeon instead of just destroying it in the hopes that OblivAeon would ignore it then.  (I just realized Deadline's plan was basically to have the Earth play dead.)  I think the fact that he's in the villains' bracket despite using his hero name indicates that the transition is still taking place, and this contest would be a great place to show his transformation into a hero.

My next priority was having one member from each hero team (Freedom Five, Dark Watch, Prime Wardens, and Void Guard) in the Final Round.  I'm not sure to what extent people are fans of hero teams as opposed to just individual heroes in the Sentinel Comics Publishing universe, but it seemed like the writers would have wanted to do their best to give everyone someone to root for through the end of the contest.  I mentioned in an earlier post, that this was my main reason for giving the Martial Tier to The Wraith, despite the fact that I think Mr. Fixer would win if we were just considering the combat aspect.  Writhe seems like a sure bet to win Tech Tier, with only Parse possibly threatening him (but she has no team to represent).  Tempest was my Prime Wardens representative partially because Tempest is my favorite (as I told my friend, "Tempest is my boy!  Well, technically Tempest has no gender.")  and if The Wraith won Martial Tier, that left Nightmist or Harpy as the only possible representatives for Dark Watch, and I had to give that one to the teacher rather than the student.

As far as the rest of the bracket, my main focus was on creating interesting stories, although there are a couple things I might change.  I really didn't want to have Haka lose right away (my first draft had him winning the Champion Tier, since he basically can't die, but then I realized these aren't going to be fights to the death, so it became much less of a factor), but Ra vs Fanatic seemed too good to pass up, especially just before their touching scene in the OblivAeon event.  I think Fanatic is capable of going toe-to-toe with Legacy, and with her passion, she's not going to give up, while Legacy would be willing to give her the win.  Despite Void Guard being supposedly OP, I also wanted to set up a Tempest vs Tachyon rematch.  Finally, I figured Tempest would beat Fanatic if only because lightning beats flying.

Tech Tier seemed like the easiest to fill in to me, and there seems to be a lot of agreement with that one on here.  I don't see how Bunker could possibly do anything to Writhe.  Benchmark vs Absolute Zero is basically showing off the cool new suit vs the old cold suit and they wouldn't want their new hero losing right away.  Unity vs Omnitron-U could be a little tricky since they wouldn't want to fight each other, but if they did, Unity could literally rip Omnitron apart.  Sky-Scraper is awesome, but Parse would find some weakness and take her down.

The main question with Mystic Tier was Nightmist vs Harpy or Doctor Medico vs Idealist?  I originally had Idealist taking the whole tier (she's another of my favorites and ridiculously powerful) but then I decided someone from Dark Watch needed to take this tier.  Also, the teacher vs student matchup seemed more interesting than the father vs daughter matchup.  Doctor Medico just wouldn't do anything to hurt his daughter, which makes for a boring fight.  For the rest of the tier, we know Argent Adept vs Visionary is canon, so that's basically all there is to it.  Another reason I had Nightmist win this tier was to make the impact losing her even greater.

I'll spare people my Martial Tier analysis, since I talked about it at length in a previous post.

The problem with the Conqueror Tier is that Progeny could probably easily take the whole thing, but that would be boring.  The Progeny event just happened not too long ago, he's about to be coming back with OblivAeon, and he doesn't talk.  As those of us unlocking the Freedom Five variants right now know, there's only so much Progeny people can take.  There's no way Apostate can beat him, but Citizen Dawn is both extremely powerful and I think popular, so she seemed the best choice to both beat him and take the tier.  I don't think Chokepoint could do much to Infinitor since he doesn't use any metal.  Zhu Long could probably destroy Kaargra if he tried, but I don't think he wants to be fighting here and would rather just go home, whereas this is Kaargra's thing.  Infinitor's manifestations are then too much for Kaargra to handle (although the panels of her fighting off hordes of them would look pretty sweet) and we're left with Infinitor vs Citizen Dawn.  He should ask K.N.Y.F.E. what happens when you bring light-based weapons to fight Citizen Dawn.

Between his popularity and lack of real challengers, it's pretty obvious that Baron Blade wins the Cunning Tier.  What is The Chairman even doing here?  I'm assuming Jansa didn't bring the whole Organization.  Without that, he's just a guy who's in excellent shape for how old he is.  Miss Information is the only other real threat here, but Baron Blade would beat her because of popularity if nothing else.

Lifeline obviously had to win the Eldritch Tier if I wanted him to win the whole tournament.  Getting to fight other blood magic-based enemies fit well.  I'm really not sure how Biomancer beats Isis (Isis by herself without the rest of the Ennead wouldn't be too much of a threat, but what can Biomancer even do in combat?  Maybe it's not really Biomancer, but a fleshchild with combat skills.) but I wanted to set up Gloomweaver vs Biomancer as a nod to the ongoing battle in the meta-narrative of the Letters Page.  Maybe that's a thing in the Sentinel Comics Publishing universe too.

Finally, the Bruiser Tier is the one I'm least sure about.  I had Spite win to give The Wraith a rematch against her nemesis in the finals and because based on the card game decks, I think he's the hardest of these villains (he's the only one who's not part of Vengeance mode).  Bugbear should beat Proletariat no problem and it would look cool to see the savage beast tearing through a bunch of clones.  For the rest I went with the idea that Plague Rat is immune to The Operative's poisons, but I think I would change this.  For one, I think the writers would have The Operative at least make it to the end of the tier if not win it, because she's probably the most interesting of this bunch and probably has a lot of fans.  I also might have Fright Train beat Plague Rat.  Being able to communicate is important to break up the monotony of battle after battle, and while neither of them are great at this, train puns are a slightly higher form of communication than growling.

Sorry for how long this was, but I love talking about Sentinels stuff.  If anyone still has questions or comments after all that, please ask!

I actually typed up my full analysis on the email I sent them, so here it is.

(Warning: this is REALLY LONG. If you don’t care, feel free to skip it, but if you do plan on reading, well… be warned.)

In the first round, Ra defeats Haka and Fanatic defeats Legacy. I’m not necessarily sure how, but the opportunity for Ra and Fanatic to fight each other is too good to pass up.

I had Mainstay defeat Tachyon, as a chance to show off the Void Guard’s newly-obtained power. Additionally, Tachyon is weaker after her fight with Progeny. However, Tempest is REALLY powerful. Not enough to defeat Fanatic, but still. Thus, Fanatic takes Champion Tier.

I figure that Parse is the Batman of the SC Multiverse, in the “given enough prep time, she can beat anyone” sense. And she’s seen Sky-Scraper fight plenty, having helped rescue her and all. Writhe, on the other hand, is unpredictable and weird, so he takes Tech Tier.

We know Argent Adept exorcises Visionary, so that matchup has to happen. NightMist vs. Harpy is also too enticing to pass up, from a narrative standpoint, but NightMist would win through experience. She takes Mystic Tier.

Martial Tier is weird. Mister Fixer SHOULD dominate it, but there is no way a “Lover’s Feud” between Setback and ExPatriette DIDN’T happen. Unfortunately, the luck that carried him TO that fight would probably run out before it could carry him THROUGH it, so ExPatriette takes Martial Tier.

In Conqueror Tier, there were some weird matchups. Since it’s unlikely that Progeny was at full power, he likely got shot down. I imagine he defeated Apostate to show that he was still in the game, but then Dawn annihilated him to show her superiority, leading her to take Conqueror Tier.

Cunning Tier was also weird. Baron Blade was strong, of course. He got to go up against the Chairman in a battle of wits, and prove that he has greater short-term planning, if not long-term viability. Given that Miss Information’s reality warping outclasses Glamour’s illusions, she would be the only competitor for Blade; I almost had her take it, but I decided on Blade eventually.

Eldritch Tier was pretty easy. Lifeline was the star of the show, and pitting him against the other Blood Mage, Bathory, and the other villain/hero, Akash’Thriya, were the best sources of drama/character development available. I considered putting him against Biomancer, but figured Akash’Thriya would do well against him.

Bruiser Tier is where most of the problems were. Fright Train would probably beat Plague Rat, being engineered for durability and power, but The Operative’s pure skill and agility would win the day. Bugbear would destroy Proletariat, feeding from destroying his clones while whittling away at his endurance. Against Heartbreaker, however, he would have trouble scoring a hit. Heartbreaker would turn the tables and play the long game, tiring him out and killing him with the metaphorical 1000 paper cuts. Plus, he has a similar game plan to the Operative, so seeing them go at it would be cool. She’s better, though, so she would win Bruiser Tier.

I think most of the finals speak for themselves. Dawn beats Writhe. Lifeline beats Operative. (He popped Gloomweaver like a blood balloon! He could do it!) Lifeline vs. Dawn would be tough, but… again, he single-handedly disassociated Rotting God Gloomy. He could probably pull it out, but it would be tough. It helps that they are not on Earth, and she doesn’t have her Citizens to back her up. Plus, having Lifeline come out on top – and therefore prove himself as a valuable asset for the heroes – seems like a reasonable ending for the story.
